method: Highest-conviction dossiers as of the Fri 2026-09-11 close, ranked by conviction then ticker. Levels are anchored to each name's real 52-week range.

ideas.why: Oracle reaffirmed roughly $95bn of AI capex on its Sep 10 print and named Dell as a beneficiary; Dell closed +11.98% at 567.29, a fresh 52-week high, on top of the $95bn AI-server backlog it disclosed on Sep 2.
bull: Record $95.0bn AI-server backlog disclosed Sep 2, with the order pipeline still widening
RBC initiated coverage Sep 11 at Outperform with a $640 target, ~13% above Friday's close
Oracle's capex pledge converts AI announcements into hardware purchase orders, and Dell and HPE are the named suppliers
bear: Server assembly is a thin-margin business: backlog dollars convert to far less gross profit than the headline suggests
Up 415% off its 52-week low of 110.22 — positioning is crowded and a single capex wobble unwinds it fast
A Sep 16 rate hike would hit the most-extended momentum names first
ideas.inv: Thesis breaks if hyperscaler or Oracle capex guidance is cut, or the backlog stops converting to revenue.
ideas.thesis: A (85.5/100). It closed AT its 52-week high, which is the worst possible entry. Let it digest: wait for a pullback toward 545 that holds, or a weekly close above 568 on continued volume, and size small into the Sep 16 Fed decision.

ideas.why: Rose 2.49% to 516.13, within 11.7% of its 52-week high, as the AI-infrastructure bid broadened past Nvidia. The MI-series is now a credible second source at exactly the moment hyperscalers want one.
bull: Hyperscalers actively want a second accelerator source, and AMD is the only merchant alternative at scale
Server CPU share gains continue to compound quietly alongside the AI story
+2.49% on Sep 11 shows it participates in the capex read-through
bear: Software ecosystem still lags CUDA by a wide margin
Valuation leaves little room — the reverse-DCF is not meaningful here, so the 48 is a judgement call
Gross margins on accelerators sit well below Nvidia's
ideas.inv: Thesis breaks if MI-series design wins slip or it closes below 454.2.
ideas.thesis: B (71.2/100). It has tripled off its 149.85 low, so the easy money is gone. Wait for a close above ~530 that holds, then buy near 500.6; avoid adding in the two sessions around the Sep 16 FOMC.

ideas.why: Rose 5.61% to 199.59 in a targeted rotation into networking — Cisco +3.1%, Ciena +4.5%, F5 +3.2%, Viavi +4.3% the same session. Money is buying the switching layer of the AI build, not tech broadly.
bull: Best-in-class Ethernet switching share as AI clusters standardise on Ethernet over InfiniBand
Sits only 7.1% below its 52-week high of 214.89 with genuine earnings behind the move, not multiple expansion alone
Gross margins far above the server assemblers benefiting from the same capex wave
bear: Customer concentration in a small number of hyperscalers
Merchant silicon competition from Broadcom-based white-box switching compresses pricing over time
Friday's 5.6% move was a sector rotation it did not earn alone
ideas.inv: Thesis breaks on evidence of hyperscalers shifting to white-box switching, or a close below the stop.
ideas.thesis: B+ (75.9/100). The move was sector-wide rather than Arista-specific, so it can give back quickly. Wait for it to hold above ~197 for a few sessions, or buy the entry near 193.6 if the networking bid persists past the FOMC.

ideas.why: Added 0.64% to 1698.30, still 15.1% below its 52-week high. Every leading-edge wafer in the AI build requires its lithography, but orders are lumpy and the stock has lagged the chain it enables.
bull: Monopoly on EUV lithography — there is literally no alternative supplier
Leading-edge capacity expansion is the physical precondition for every AI accelerator shipped
High-NA transition extends the monopoly another technology generation
bear: Order intake is lumpy and a single quarter can badly miss
Export-control exposure to China revenue remains a policy risk
15% off the high while the demand story strengthened — the market is questioning order timing
ideas.inv: Thesis breaks on a leading-edge capex cut from TSMC or Samsung, or a close below 1528.5.
ideas.thesis: B- (68.4/100). Lagging is not the same as cheap here. Buy near 1647.3 on weakness; a close back above ~1750 would confirm the semicap group is following the logic names higher.

ideas.why: Barely moved (+0.32% to 361.99) despite the Oracle capex news, and still sits 26.9% below its 52-week high of 495 — the widest gap between disclosed AI numbers and share price in the book.
bull: Its September quarter showed AI semiconductor revenue growing triple digits with a multi-year AI guide stepping up sharply
Custom accelerator programmes with hyperscalers are the direct beneficiary of the capex Oracle just reaffirmed
27% below its high while DELL makes new highs on the same underlying demand
bear: VMware software integration carries execution and customer-churn risk
Leverage from the VMware deal matters more if the Fed hikes on Sep 16
Custom-silicon revenue is lumpy and programme-dependent
ideas.inv: Thesis breaks if custom-accelerator design wins are lost to a competitor, or on a close below 318.6.
ideas.thesis: B- (67.7/100). The dislocation is the point, but it needs a trigger. Accumulate near 351.1 on weakness; add only on a daily close back above ~375 that shows the custom-silicon story is being re-rated rather than ignored.

ideas.why: Closed 137.35, just 1.1% below its 52-week high of 138.89, after joining CVX and VLO at annual highs on Sep 9. Pure upstream leverage to the Hormuz premium.
bull: Highest upstream torque to crude of the three energy majors held here
Hit a 52-week high on Sep 9 as Brent cleared $101 for the first time since May
Low-cost, long-duration resource base with disciplined capital return
bear: No refining hedge — a pure price bet with no downstream offset
1.1% from its 52-week high on a geopolitical premium
A Hormuz resolution would hit this hardest of the energy names
ideas.inv: Thesis breaks on Brent below $80 or a close below 123.6.
ideas.thesis: B+ (78.2/100). The purest oil-price beta in the book and it is at its high. Wait for a pullback to near 131.9 rather than buying the breakout; require Brent to hold above $95 or the whole setup is invalid.

ideas.why: Fell 1.02% to 206.74, 11.6% below its high. Security spending holds up better than most software, but the multiple still carries rate risk.
bull: Single-agent platform architecture wins consolidation deals
Security budgets are the last thing cut in a slowdown
Net retention remains among the best in software
bear: Premium multiple leaves no room for execution error
-1.02% on a +0.86% day is mild relative weakness
Microsoft bundling pressure on endpoint is structural
ideas.inv: Invalidated on a close below 184.0, or if the reason for owning it stops being true.
ideas.thesis: The best pure-play security platform, priced accordingly. A rate-driven drawdown is the entry, not the exit.

ideas.why: Set a fresh 52-week high at 214.06 on Sep 11 — its second in three sessions — closing +0.61%. Brent settling above $101 on Sep 9 for the first time since May was the trigger.
bull: Fresh 52-week high on Sep 11, the second in three sessions — sustained institutional buying
Strongest balance sheet among the majors, so it compounds through the cycle
Permian and Guyana volume growth is independent of the oil price spike
bear: Trading 1.5% from its 52-week high on a premium the market may not keep paying
Friday's 2.5% Brent pullback on diplomacy hopes is the direct risk
Energy's two-week leadership makes it a crowded rotation
ideas.inv: Thesis breaks on Brent sustainably below $80, or a close below 190.5.
ideas.thesis: B+ (79.5/100). It just printed a 52-week high, so patience matters more than conviction. Buy near 205.5 on a pullback that holds; chasing a name at its high on a geopolitical premium into an FOMC is the error to avoid.

ideas.why: Slipped 0.32% to 675.74 but holds within 4.3% of its 52-week high — remarkable relative strength for a cyclical with the 2-year at 4.63% and a hike likely.
bull: Holding within 4.3% of its 52-week high while rate-sensitive cyclicals de-rate
Precision agriculture technology is a genuine recurring-revenue transition
Analyst support is strong, with Baird and Evercore ISI both at Outperform with $800 and $813 targets
bear: Farm income is under pressure and equipment is the most deferrable purchase there is
A Sep 16 hike raises financing costs for the customer, not just the company
4.3% from the high leaves little room if the ag cycle turns
ideas.inv: Thesis breaks on a farm-income-driven order collapse or a close below 618.3.
ideas.thesis: B (74.3/100). It is holding near highs despite the rate backdrop, which is the bull case and also the risk. Buy near 655.5 on a pullback; a close below 620 would say the farm-economy bear case is finally biting.

ideas.why: Rose 3.96% to 425.37, one of Friday's stronger large-cap moves, on the same Oracle capex read-through — data centres need electrical distribution before they need chips. Sits 11.0% below its 52-week high.
bull: +3.96% on Sep 11 as data-centre electrical content was re-rated alongside Dell and Vertiv
Electrical infrastructure is a physical bottleneck for AI capacity, with multi-year backlogs
Diversified across aerospace, vehicle and industrial end markets, not a pure AI bet
bear: Reverse-DCF implies a demanding long-run growth rate for an industrial
Cyclical exposure if a Sep 16 hike slows broader industrial activity
11% below its high despite the strongest end-market demand in its history
ideas.inv: Thesis breaks on data-centre order deceleration or a close below 378.6.
ideas.thesis: B (71.9/100). A strong move without a company-specific catalyst can fade. Buy near 412.6; require it to hold above 415 through the FOMC week to confirm the electrification bid is durable rather than a one-day sympathy trade.

ideas.why: Rose 3.61% to 957.27 on the data-centre power theme, though it remains 20.0% below its 52-week high of 1195.94. Gas turbines and grid equipment are the hard constraint on AI capacity.
bull: +3.61% on Sep 11 as the data-centre power constraint was re-rated
Gas turbine order backlogs extend years out with pricing power
Grid equipment demand is structural and independent of the AI cycle
bear: Very high valuation even after a 20% drawdown — the 45 is a judgement score
Execution risk in the offshore wind segment continues
Long-cycle equipment orders are vulnerable if financing costs rise on Sep 16
ideas.inv: Thesis breaks on turbine order cancellations or a close below 842.4.
ideas.thesis: B- (65.2/100). It moved 3.6% on sympathy rather than news. Buy near 928.5; require a close above ~1000 to confirm the power-equipment bid is real. This is the most expensive way in the book to own electrification.

ideas.why: Rose 1.77% to 338.50 in Friday's Communication Services-led rebound, still 17.2% below its 52-week high. Cheapest of the mega-cap platforms on the reverse-DCF despite owning its own AI silicon and model stack.
bull: Owns the full stack — TPUs, models, cloud and distribution — which no competitor matches
Comm Services led Friday's rebound, and Alphabet was a primary beneficiary
Reverse-DCF implies the lowest growth burden of the mega-cap platforms
bear: Search monetisation faces genuine disruption from conversational AI interfaces
Regulatory and antitrust overhang persists across multiple jurisdictions
Capex intensity has stepped up sharply without clear incremental return yet
ideas.inv: Thesis breaks on evidence of search query-share loss showing up in revenue, or a close below 304.7.
ideas.thesis: B- (68.8/100). Buy near 328.3 rather than chasing Friday's bounce. A close above ~350 would confirm the Comm Services rotation has legs; below 305 the search-disruption bear case is being priced.

ideas.why: Rose 0.92% to 1029.18, 10.8% below its 52-week high. Capital markets activity benefits from the AI capex boom financing itself — Oracle's spending has to be funded somewhere.
bull: Debt and equity issuance to fund AI infrastructure flows straight to fee revenue
Higher rates support net interest income in its financing book
10.8% below its high while the deal environment improves
bear: Capital markets revenue is inherently cyclical and lumpy
A rate hike that slows the economy closes the issuance window
Excluded from the reverse-DCF — the 64 is judgement, not computed
ideas.inv: Thesis breaks if the issuance window closes or it closes below 916.0. Valuation is a judgement score — investment banks are excluded from the DCF for the same reason as JPM.
ideas.thesis: B (72.2/100). Less directly rate-levered than JPM, so the Sep 16 event matters less. Buy near 998.3 on weakness; a close above ~1075 would confirm the capital-markets recovery is being re-rated rather than just hoped for.
